"""A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * The graph is kept as a single dict ``_deps`` mapping
        task name -> set(names of that task's DIRECT dependencies).
    Registering a task with no dependencies stores an empty set.
  * "task depends_on dep" means ``dep`` must run BEFORE ``task``; it is
    recorded by adding ``dep`` to ``_deps[task]``.
  * Everything is deterministic: there is no randomness, wall-clock, or
    network use anywhere, and any ordering exposed to callers is sorted.

Public API (do not rename without updating callers):
  add_task(name), add_dependency(task, depends_on), remove_task(name),
  tasks(), dependencies(name), has_cycle(), topo_order(),
  ready(done), waves(), run(runner)

Cycle safety:
  * add_dependency refuses -- with ValueError and without mutating the
    graph -- any edge that would make a task depend on itself or that would
    close a cycle (``depends_on`` already reaches ``task`` through existing
    edges), so the graph is acyclic by construction.
  * has_cycle() additionally guards the stored ``_deps`` state (e.g. after
    direct tampering), reporting whether a cycle is present; topo_order(),
    waves() and run() raise ValueError if one is.
"""

import bisect


class Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        # name -> set of direct dependency names
        self._deps = {}

    # ----- graph construction --------------------------------------------
    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def add_dependency(self, task, depends_on):
        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new.

        Cycle-safe: raises ValueError -- leaving the graph unchanged -- when
        the recorded edge would close a cycle, i.e. when ``task`` is
        ``depends_on`` (a task cannot depend on itself) or ``depends_on``
        already reaches ``task`` through existing edges."""
        if task == depends_on:
            raise ValueError(
                "a task cannot depend on itself: " + task
            )
        if self._reaches(depends_on, task):
            raise ValueError(
                "refusing to create a dependency cycle: " + task
                + " cannot depend on " + depends_on + " because "
                + depends_on + " already depends on " + task
                + ", directly or transitively"
            )
        self.add_task(task)
        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    def remove_task(self, name):
        """Remove ``name`` from the graph together with every edge that
        references it: ``name``'s own dependency entries AND every other
        task's direct dependency on ``name``. No other task is touched --
        a task that only appeared as one of ``name``'s dependencies stays
        registered (as an isolated task if it now has none).

        Raises KeyError if ``name`` is not a registered task. Removal only
        deletes a task and edges, so it can never create a cycle and needs
        no cycle guard."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            raise KeyError(name)
        del self._deps[name]
        for deps in self._deps.values():
            deps.discard(name)

    # ----- graph reads ----------------------------------------------------
    def tasks(self):
        """Sorted list of all registered task names."""
        return sorted(self._deps.keys())

    def dependencies(self, name):
        """Sorted list of ``name``'s DIRECT dependencies."""
        return sorted(self._deps[name])

    def ready(self, done):
        """Sorted list of tasks that can start next: registered tasks that
        are not in ``done`` and whose every DIRECT dependency is in ``done``.

        ``done`` is any iterable of already-completed task names. Names in
        ``done`` that are not registered tasks are ignored, and so is a task
        listed in ``done`` even if its dependencies are not -- completed
        tasks never come back. A task with no dependencies is ready as soon
        as it is not itself in ``done``."""
        done = set(done)
        return sorted(
            name for name, deps in self._deps.items()
            if name not in done and done.issuperset(deps)
        )

    # ----- cycle safety ---------------------------------------------------
    def _reaches(self, start, target):
        """True iff ``target`` is reachable from ``start`` through at least
        one existing dependency edge (an edge points from a task to one of
        its direct dependencies). This guards add_dependency: recording
        ``task -> depends_on`` would close a cycle exactly when
        ``depends_on`` can already reach ``task``."""
        seen = set()
        stack = [start]
        while stack:
            name = stack.pop()
            if name in seen or name not in self._deps:
                continue
            seen.add(name)
            for dep in self._deps[name]:
                if dep == target:
                    return True
                stack.append(dep)
        return False

    def has_cycle(self):
        """True iff the current graph contains a cycle: a task that depends
        on itself, directly or through a chain of other tasks.

        add_dependency's guards keep the graph acyclic by construction; this
        method defensively reports on the stored ``_deps`` state."""
        return len(self._kahn_order()) != len(self._deps)

    # ----- ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    def _kahn_order(self):
        """Kahn's algorithm over working copies of ``_deps`` (the stored
        adjacency is never mutated). Returns the order produced; when a cycle
        prevents some tasks from ever becoming free this is a strict prefix
        of ALL registered tasks, which lets callers detect the cycle."""
        # indegree = number of dependencies not yet placed; dependents maps
        # each dependency to the tasks waiting on it (both derived from _deps).
        remaining = {name: len(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        dependents = {name: set() for name in self._deps}
        for task, deps in self._deps.items():
            for dep in deps:
                dependents[dep].add(task)

        # The frontier holds tasks whose dependencies are all placed; it is
        # kept sorted so popping the front always emits the alphabetically
        # first task that is free right now.
        frontier = sorted(
            name for name, degree in remaining.items() if degree == 0
        )
        order = []
        while frontier:
            name = frontier.pop(0)
            order.append(name)
            for task in dependents[name]:
                remaining[task] -= 1
                if remaining[task] == 0:
                    bisect.insort(frontier, task)
        return order

    def topo_order(self):
        """Return ALL registered tasks in dependency order: every task appears
        after each task it (directly or transitively) depends on.

        Deterministic: whenever several tasks are simultaneously free to run
        (all of their dependencies have already been placed), they are emitted
        in alphabetical order. This is Kahn's algorithm with an
        alphabetically-sorted frontier, computed from working copies of
        ``_deps`` so the stored adjacency is never mutated.

        Raises ValueError if the current graph contains a cycle (which the
        add_dependency guards prevent from being built through the public
        API), in which case no such ordering exists.
        """
        order = self._kahn_order()
        if len(order) != len(self._deps):
            cyclic = sorted(set(self._deps) - set(order))
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no topological order exists: "
                + ", ".join(cyclic)
            )
        return order

    def waves(self):
        """Layering of the whole graph into sorted levels.

        Level 0 is exactly the registered tasks that have no dependencies.
        Level k is the tasks whose every DIRECT dependency appears in an
        earlier level (some level < k). Because the graph is acyclic (see
        the cycle-safety contract), a task's level is 1 + the largest level
        among its direct dependencies (0 when it has none) -- the earliest
        level it could run at -- so every registered task appears in
        exactly one level and the levels partition ``tasks()``.

        Deterministic: computed over the stored adjacency without mutating
        it, and every level is returned sorted alphabetically.

        Raises ValueError if the current graph contains a cycle (which the
        add_dependency guards prevent from being built through the public
        API), since then no such layering exists.
        """
        # A topological order guarantees every task is visited only after
        # its direct dependencies, so their levels are known when needed.
        order = self.topo_order()  # raises ValueError if a cycle is present
        wave_of = {}
        levels = {}
        for name in order:
            deps = self._deps[name]
            if deps:
                wave = 1 + max(wave_of[dep] for dep in deps)
            else:
                wave = 0
            wave_of[name] = wave
            levels.setdefault(wave, []).append(name)
        return [sorted(levels[k]) for k in sorted(levels)]

    # ----- execution -------------------------------------------------------
    def run(self, runner):
        """Execute every registered task once, in dependency order, and
        return a dict mapping every task name to its status.

        Walks ``topo_order()`` and, for each task whose dependencies all
        turned out fine, calls ``runner(name)``. If that call raises any
        exception the exception is swallowed, the task's status becomes
        ``"failed"`` (the raising call's return value, if any, is
        discarded), and every task that depends on it -- directly or
        transitively -- gets status ``"skipped"`` with ``runner`` never
        called for it. Tasks that do not depend on a failed task still run
        normally and are ``"ok"``.

        The propagation needs no lookahead: every dependency precedes its
        task in ``topo_order()``, so by the time a task is reached all of
        its dependencies already have a status. A task is skipped exactly
        when at least one of its DIRECT dependencies has status ``"failed"``
        or ``"skipped"`` -- the latter itself marks a failed task further
        down -- which makes the direct-or-transitive rule above fall out of
        one pass. ``runner`` is called at most once per task; its return
        values are otherwise ignored.

        The returned dict keys -- one per registered task, in execution
        (topological) order -- map to ``"ok"``, ``"failed"`` or
        ``"skipped"``, and the whole outcome is deterministic: repeat runs
        over an unchanged graph call ``runner`` identically and return the
        same dict. ``_deps`` is never mutated.

        Raises ValueError if the current graph contains a cycle (which the
        add_dependency guards prevent from being built through the public
        API), since then no order to run in exists; in that case no runner
        call is made.
        """
        status = {}
        for name in self.topo_order():
            if any(
                status.get(dep) in ("failed", "skipped")
                for dep in self._deps[name]
            ):
                status[name] = "skipped"
                continue
            try:
                runner(name)
            except Exception:
                status[name] = "failed"
            else:
                status[name] = "ok"
        return status
